main_text.p: timas ciuitates descendens, & lingua & animo Græcus fuit. Quumque accidisset, ut eo tempore nos quoque in maritimis Asiæ locis uersaremur, philosophiæ amore ad nos sponte uenit, qui multo plura nobis attulit, quàm acceperat. Sic Plato Magiam Zoroastris Chaldæi nihil aliud esse scripsit in Alcibiade, quàm diuini cultus scientiam, qua filios Persarum reges erudiebant, ut ad exemplar mundanæ Reipub. suam ipsi regere Rempub. addiscerent. In Epinomide deinde Chaldæis & Ægyptiis propter æstiui temporis in utraque regione serenitatem, ubi stellæ omnes clarè cernuntur, semper Astronomiæ tribuit inuentionem, Chaldæumque quempiam auctorem nominum fuisse perhibet. Nam de Planeta Veneris verba faciens, ajt: Lucifer, qui & Vesper, Stella τῆς Αφεσδίτης esse dicitur. quod Chaldæo nominum auctori valdè congruit. stella enim, quæ proxima sub Sole occupat, sphæram, φωσφόρος Græcis dicta, idem planè sonat, quod Hebræis noghah, Babyloniis veró noghehá, quod est, Lucifer, siue Stella rutilans ac splendens, &c. Verum enimuerò tam altas radices in corda hominum, maximè Principum, qui rerum potiti sunt, antequam Euangelii iubar aureos splendoris sui radios in totam orbem terrarum dispersisset, egit

page.notes: The line "in totam orbem terrarum dispersisset" is partly obscured by a printer's ink smudge; "totam" is read as "totum" in the scan's inked region and "dispersisset" is partly overprinted, so the word "dispersisset" is marked as doubtful. Greek words "τῆς Αφεσδίτης" and "φωσφόρος" are read from the scan and may contain errors. The line "Lucifer, qui & Vesper" is italic in the original. A wrap-around blot appears in the lower left of the page; the faint mark at lower left is not printed text. The signature "N 5" is printed at the foot and is also recorded in the footnote position. The "egit" line is the last full line on the page and is not followed by a catchword.
